description: A small hand-written Inspect log (log.json, one epoch) that pins the rulings settled 10-10 (R7I, R8-4). Its model acme/gpt x becomes model:acme/gpt%20x (R7I-8). Of eval.model_roles, grader and grader_b share one judge model, written once, and attacker is no judge (R7I-16). The epochs reducer collect has no AEF value: with one epoch it is kept in run.json's ext (R7I-14). Without stats.started_at, eval.created stands for the start, listed last in imported.asserted (R7I-17). An empty explanation and empty content give no blob (R7I-17). The NaN member of a map gets no score (R7I-13). A sample stopped by a token limit gives the reason "token limit 1000", and an error message of 5,074 characters is cut to its first 4096 (R7I-12). A limit is written from its value alone, as ECMAScript's Number::toString writes it: 1000.0 gives "token limit 1000", 1e16 "token limit 10000000000000000", 1e21 "message limit 1e+21"; an error with an empty message gives "Inspect recorded an error without a message" (R8-4). Two roles that land on one AEF role and model are added together; without stats.model_usage, the run's usage comes from role_usage (R7I-10). A results entry with no metric is a plain mean entry, with nothing of Inspect's to compare (R7I-15). Sample h's content that is not text (an input of messages, a ModelOutput with members out of order, 1.0 and 2.50, and keys whose UTF-16 order differs from their code-point order) becomes blobs serialized by JCS, RFC 8785, so their names depend on the values alone (IN-8, settled 10-10). Each file under refusals/ changes one thing the page refuses: an empty limit type, a NaN limit (R8-4), a NaN inside content that is not text, which JCS cannot write (IN-8).
